beats.lead: Sega's answer to Mario did not start as a hedgehog
beats.note: Sega's 1990 internal contest to find a new mascot drew around 200 submitted designs.

beats.context: Roughly how many characters Sega's own staff submitted before anyone had heard of Sonic.

beats.lead: The rabbit did not survive contact with the actual game
beats.text: It picked up objects with its ears and threw them at enemies, and that slowed everything down.
beats.note: Programmer Yuji Naka said plainly that game speed could not be maintained with that action.

beats.text: So the choice narrowed to two animals that roll into a ball: an armadillo, or a hedgehog.
beats.note: The hedgehog won because its quills looked like an attack. The armadillo's shell just looked like armour.

beats.text: The winning design was not even new. It was an old doodle Ohshima had already thrown away.

beats.line: The mascot that beat Mario started out as a rabbit nobody kept.
